person.name: Kanishk Dubey
person.intro: I build at the intersection of AI, connected hardware, and the web. Turning curiosity into systems people can actually use.
person.bio: I’m Kanishk, a BS–MS student in Computer Science & Data Analytics at IIT Patna. I work across AI-assisted products, IoT prototypes, and research — following a problem from the first question to a working system.

projects.title: ESC
projects.subtitle: A clearer next step in learning.
projects.summary: An adaptive study companion connecting questions, specialist help, practice, and personalised study plans in one workspace.
projects.imageAlt: ESC homepage showing its learning companion and specialist workflow
projects.recognition: Runner-up · Hack & Jam 2026; 2nd rank · Code for Community 2026
projects.problem: Studying often means switching between a chatbot, notes, practice questions, and a planner. ESC brings those activities into a connected flow, so a question leads to useful practice and a plan for what comes next.
projects.approach: I worked on the personalised learning experience: combining performance signals with topic-level guidance and relevant resources. The application includes conversational assistance, a specialist studio, and an adaptive learning workspace.

decisions.title: Keep the conversation central
decisions.body: Chat is the quickest way to ask for help. Structured workspaces provide a separate place to inspect plans, practice, and recorded progress.

decisions.title: Connect practice to planning
decisions.body: Assessment results inform topic mastery and the next study plan. Deterministic scoring keeps recorded performance separate from generated explanations.

decisions.title: Make sources visible
decisions.body: Uploaded material and web research provide context for specialist responses. Source visibility supports review; it is not a guarantee of accuracy.

projects.outcome: Runner-up at Hack & Jam, Anjuman College of Engineering and Technology, on 2 August 2026. The event’s community partner was GDG Nagpur.
projects.limitations: Actively developed prototype. A September local audit found live generation unavailable in that environment; provider reliability and complete export testing remain ongoing work.
projects.next: Connect the source library, practice tools, and saved plans more consistently, and improve reliable generation.

projects.title: AgroBot
projects.subtitle: A little hardware. A closer look at soil.
projects.summary: A compact soil-monitoring device with Wi-Fi telemetry, a live dashboard, and local alerts that keep working offline.
projects.problem: Soil conditions are difficult to track remotely. AgroBot explores a simple way to sense moisture, signal unsafe conditions locally, and bring readings to a dashboard.
projects.approach: I designed and built a compact prototype around a NodeMCU V3, resistive soil-moisture sensor, and piezoelectric buzzer. HTTP telemetry pairs current values with a seven-day trend view.

decisions.title: Simplify the board architecture
decisions.body: Moving from Arduino Uno plus a separate ESP8266 to NodeMCU combines sensing and Wi-Fi on one board.

decisions.title: Keep an offline feedback path
decisions.body: The buzzer signals dry or waterlogged conditions independently of the network.

decisions.title: Show change over time
decisions.body: A current reading gives immediate context. Historical readings show how conditions evolve.

projects.outcome: Built as a Capstone-I prototype at IIT Patna. My résumé documents hardware, enclosure, telemetry, and dashboard work.
projects.limitations: The public README marks server/database integration and the final end-to-end test as pending. No measured farm deployment or water-saving result is claimed.
projects.next: Validate the complete data path and compare sensor behaviour across soil conditions before field deployment.

projects.title: Drishti
projects.subtitle: Make every mark traceable.
projects.summary: A human-in-the-loop marking platform connecting answer-sheet intake, AI-assisted evaluation, moderation, and QR-verifiable records.
projects.problem: Answer evaluation needs readable capture, correct script-to-record mapping, and a way to review differences between human and AI assessments.
projects.approach: My work covers the research manuscript, literature review, cost modelling, and an ESP32-S3 CAM capture-rig architecture. The optical design considers lens calibration, lighting, and capture quality before evaluation.

decisions.title: Keep humans in the decision loop
decisions.body: Assisted evaluation is separate from final judgement. Moderation makes disagreements visible and preserves a review trail.

decisions.title: Start with capture quality
decisions.body: Unreadable input undermines every later step. The capture design considers optical budget, calibration, and dual-LED illumination.

decisions.title: Separate modelling from validation
decisions.body: Analytical estimates guide the prototype but require empirical evaluation before operational claims.

projects.outcome: Research manuscript in preparation, with a documented capture architecture and evaluation workflow. Team and upstream credit are preserved.
projects.limitations: The software works with uploaded or browser-captured answer sheets. The repository documents the physical camera provider as a planned, uncertified integration; a separate team post describes a hackathon capture-system build. The manuscript is in preparation, and measured grading accuracy and hardware performance remain to be validated.
projects.next: Evaluate capture quality and review outcomes using an appropriate, permissioned test dataset.

projects.title: COMET
projects.subtitle: Specialists, working together.
projects.summary: A multi-agent research and planning workspace coordinating specialist tasks, API integrations, evidence, and structured reports.
projects.problem: Research and planning cross tools and specialisms. A useful agent system coordinates those handoffs while retaining context.
projects.approach: I worked on an orchestration layer, API adapters, retry logic, and monitoring hooks. The workspace brings together business and student workflows, uploaded sources, and specialist chat.

decisions.title: Give each agent a responsibility
decisions.body: Specialist roles make intermediate outputs easier to inspect and connect.

decisions.title: Treat failure as part of the workflow
decisions.body: Retries and monitoring help identify where external calls or agent steps fail.

projects.outcome: An orchestration prototype demonstrated in a live pipeline, as documented in my résumé.
projects.limitations: A collaborative prototype. Agent workflows depend on configured model providers, supported tools, and source availability.
projects.next: Make recovery and the relationship between sources, agent outputs, and saved reports easier to follow.

projects.title: Catalyst
projects.subtitle: From materials to a scientific investigation.
projects.summary: A scientific workspace for exploring materials, crystal structures, evidence graphs, and genomics through guided, AI-assisted investigations.
projects.problem: Scientific records are difficult to explore when structures, properties, source evidence, and related biological context sit in separate tools.
projects.approach: The supplied Quantathon repository presents Catalyst as a materials and genomics workspace with interactive structures, source context, and guided investigations. My résumé documents the earlier VQE exploration; that individual contribution is distinct from the capabilities of the current team workspace.

decisions.title: Keep research scope explicit
decisions.body: VQE exploration and the current materials workspace are related contexts, not interchangeable descriptions.

decisions.title: Preserve provenance
decisions.body: My individual contribution is described separately from the complete capabilities of the team repository.

projects.outcome: Finalist at RIT Quant-A-Thon 2026, held on 29–30 July, as recorded in my résumé.
projects.limitations: No quantum advantage, validated scientific discovery, or performance beyond classical limits is claimed.
projects.next: Document reproducible experiments and individual contributions alongside the corresponding project revision.

projects.title: ESC Connect
projects.subtitle: Learning, opportunity and community.
projects.summary: An ESC Buildx prototype connecting scholarship discovery, opportunities, teacher communication and attendance follow-up.
projects.problem: Students need access to opportunities and school support alongside learning resources.
projects.approach: The project explores profile-based scholarship matching, a filtered opportunities feed, school groups and signals for attendance follow-up. Text-first interaction is a focus for limited-data environments.

decisions.title: Connect information to action
decisions.body: Profiles and filters help turn an opportunity feed into a relevant next step.

decisions.title: Design for limited connectivity
decisions.body: Text-first screens and simple language make the intended workflows easier to access.

projects.outcome: A publicly available prototype and product analytics overview in the ESC Buildx repository.
projects.limitations: The README labels its benchmark figures as demo presentation data. They are not measured performance claims.
projects.next: Validate the student and teacher journeys with users and replace demonstration data with observed results.

events.title: GDG Code for Community · Second Edition
events.location: G H Raisoni College of Engineering and Management · Nagpur
events.summary: Second rank among the top five at the second edition of GDG Code for Community.
events.story: A new milestone in my hackathon journey: second rank in the top five at GDG Code for Community, second edition, on 19 September 2026. The event was held at G H Raisoni College of Engineering and Management (GHRCEMN), B-37-39/1 Wadi Link Road, Nagpur.

events.title: Faraway International Hackathon · Drishti
events.summary: Finalists at Faraway International Hackathon, presenting Drishti: a human-in-the-loop examination-evaluation platform.
events.story: Our team took Drishti to Faraway International Hackathon at Chandigarh University and finished as finalists. My contribution focused on research writing and the capture-system architecture. We built and demonstrated an examination-evaluation workflow with human review at its centre. The final-round experience strengthened both the project and our teamwork.

events.title: Build with Swytchcode
events.summary: Helping bring builders together for the Swytchcode × KNOTiC buildathon.
events.story: I was one of the organizers of Build with Swytchcode 2026. The event brought builders, mentors and judges together at the Paytm office in Noida to experiment with APIs and develop working prototypes.

events.title: Hack & Jam
events.summary: Building ESC, an adaptive learning companion, and presenting it in the final round.
events.story: We built ESC to connect student performance with personalised study plans and relevant learning resources. I worked on adaptive learning and recommendation workflows, then presented the working prototype at Hack & Jam, hosted by Anjuman College of Engineering and Technology with GDG Nagpur as community partner.

events.title: RIT Quant-A-Thon
events.summary: A 36-hour international hackathon exploring AI-assisted scientific workflows.
events.story: My first international hackathon experience brought together materials research, rapid prototyping and teamwork in Chennai. The Catalyst project connects scientific investigation with an interactive workspace. My résumé records our finalist standing and my contribution to quantum VQE exploration.

events.title: Bharatiya Antariksh Hackathon
events.summary: Exploring intelligent agriculture with AgroBot, connected sensing and data-driven insights.
events.story: I received a Certificate of Participation from the Bharatiya Antariksh Hackathon 2026, presented by ISRO. My work explored an intelligent agriculture solution, including AgroBot soil-moisture monitoring and decision support.

events.title: Webcmd Hackathon
events.summary: From individual AI answers to coordinated, evidence-based workflows.
events.story: At the Webcmd Hackathon, we built COMET: a multi-agent system that breaks goals into tasks, coordinates specialist agents and assembles structured outputs. The project explored evidence-based research and live data integration through Agentr.

events.title: IWSA Research Contest
events.summary: A survey-based study of social media and family communication.
events.story: I co-authored a study on how social media affects family communication, surveying respondents across age groups and professions. The research won first place at the Indian Women Scientist Association Nagpur chapter contest and was covered in Lokmat Times on 18 December 2021.

events.title: National Children Science Congress
events.summary: Representing the Vidarbha region at the state-level science forum.
events.story: Our research project was selected to represent Vidarbha at the state-level National Children Science Congress in Pune. This early experience introduced me to presenting research beyond the classroom.

experience.title: Freelance AI-Augmented Web Developer
experience.body: Scope, prototype, review, and deliver client websites. My workflow connects AI-assisted development with debugging, accessibility checks, deployment, and clear handover documentation.

experience.title: Sub-Coordinator
experience.body: Organised workshops on prompt engineering, AI-assisted development, Git, and CI/CD, and mentored juniors through rapid prototyping workflows.
